messages:
Noah: Heads-up 1: Aegis Health wants a short POC: SAML SSO (Azure), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with nested groups. They also pushed a security questionnaire with KMS + log retention asks. Need to assemble answers + rough Dedicated vs Hosted cost scenario by Fri.
Priya: I can draft the SAML checklist. We'll need their IdP metadata, desired ACS URL, and whether they want SP-initiated only or IdP-initiated too. Also ask if they want SAML attribute statements for groups or a JWT/claim passthrough.
Liam: On SCIM: clarify if they expect push (SCIM POST/PUT/PATCH) or periodic pulls. We support full list + incremental via lastModified filter; group push is supported but nested groups are flattened during ingest. If they need nested semantics we can provide a client-side expansion helper.
Noah: The questionnaire asks for proof of domain ownership & delegated domain claims. What's our standard flow?
Priya: Standard domain verification is DNS TXT record or email verification for a domain admin. For delegated domains we support DNS TXT + an approval workflow where an admin from the delegating domain confirms. Note caveat: automated tenant creation requires an SCIM externalId on groups or a webhook to map domain -> tenant.
Liam: RBAC mapping note: we map SCIM groups to Redwood roles via the `roleMapping` table. Example mapping: roleMapping = [{"group":"engineering","role":"engineer"},{"group":"admins","role":"org_admin"}]. If they send nested groups like payroll -> company -> employees, we will expand to members list but not preserve nesting relationships unless they include an attribute with parentGroup.
Claire: OpsBot flagged logs retention: they require 12 months of audit logs; Hosted provides 90 days by default. Dedicated/Private can meet 12 months for an additional fee. Also KMS: Hosted uses Redwood-managed encryption keys; we offer Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) in Dedicated and Private via KMS integrations.
Noah: Pricing ask from Aegis: 25k MAU, sporadic peaks (300 qps), heavy embedding usage for search. Can someone draft 3-tier estimate (POC, Production-small, Production-medium) with clear assumptions?
Liam: Draft numbers: POC (hosted): $5k/mo estimate (low traffic, limited models), Dedicated starter (2 reserved GPUs + burst) $20k/mo baseline, Production-medium (4 reserved + HA) $45k+/mo. Varies a lot with model choice and quantization. For embeddings consumption add tokens/embedding call pricing.
Priya: I'll prepare the SAML checklist and include sample attribute mapping request: we ask for `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/name`, `memberOf` or `groups` attributes, and whether they sign assertions/encrypt. Also note our SLO support adds config time.
Noah: Action list: Priya -> SAML checklist + sample SP metadata to send Aegis (ETA: tomorrow morning). Liam -> SCIM + RBAC mapping doc and sample PATCH/PUT examples (ETA: EOD tomorrow). Claire -> write the KMS/logs/gdpr note and a one-pager on Hosted vs Dedicated security differences (ETA: Thu). Noah -> assemble the quote templates and coordinate the POC call.
OpsBot: Compliance links: SOC2 report available on request; ISO27001 summary: https://redwood.example/security. CMK options documented here: https://redwood.example/ops/kms.
Priya: Quick tech question to prod: does our SCIM accept `externalId` on groups? We depend on that for tenant auto-provisioning on domain claim.
Liam: Yes, SCIM supports `externalId` on groups and users. If they want auto-provisioning, make sure their SCIM group payload includes `externalId` mapped to the tenant slug. Example group payload snippet: {"displayName":"engineering","externalId":"tenant-123","members":[{"value":"user-abc"}]}
Noah: I'll send the questionnaire + ask for IdP metadata, SCIM base URL + token, a sample group payload, and approximate token/embedding volume. Propose Wed 9am PT for the working session.
Claire: :white_check_mark: I'll also include toggles for log retention and CMK costs so we can show delta pricing.
Noah: Thanks team 1: once we have the metadata we can validate SAML and run a SCIM dry-run before the call to avoid surprises.
